dedupe_keys.name: amanzi flow and reactive transport simulator

description: Amanzi is a U.S. Department of Energy laboratory collaboration's simulator for flow and reactive transport in environmental systems. It contains parallel solvers, polyhedral meshes and the Arcos multiphysics coupling machinery. Its Alquimia interface connects geochemistry engines such as PFLOTRAN and CrunchFlow. Model definitions describe soil or rock domains and coupled processes; simulations examine groundwater movement and contaminant migration under partially saturated, nonisothermal conditions. Spatial detail follows the mesh, and temporal coverage follows the configured experiment. Source code and installation guidance are available through GitHub free under BSD-3-Clause. A limitation is that advanced coupled calculations require separate numerical and chemistry dependencies; documented applications do not establish accuracy for a new site. Amanzi supports groundwater-supply protection and waste-site remediation studies. FEHM (model-fehm) provides related subsurface modelling. The README names Nevada and Savannah River applications, but this review did not verify their input datasets or execute any model.
